subject: INITIALIZE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-02 (PB152), COBOL1727. 'Hexadecimal-alphanumeric literal' is a DEFINED TERM and the screen is written to it, not to a paraphrase: 8.3.3.2.2 gives the alphanumeric literal exactly two general formats - format 1 ("..." / '...') and format 2 (X"..." / X'...') - and 'hexadecimal-alphanumeric' names FORMAT 2, so a one-character format-1 literal such as "Z" is NOT admitted however short it is. One byte is exactly two hexadecimal digits (8.3.3.2.3 SR5). Before the screen the decoder took raw[0] for ANY shape, so INITIALIZE ALL TO "AB" silently became 'A'. The 2026-08-30 analysis that scoped this work carried the paraphrase 'a one-character alphanumeric OR one-byte hex literal', which would have shipped an under-reject; the printed page (PDF 307 / folio 277) was rendered and read to settle it. PB151's own golden pb151_options_fill was written with the format-1 spelling and is repaired to X"51" by this landing - 0x51 IS 'Q', so its expected output is unchanged byte for byte.
